questions.passage: Every morning, Darius fed the chickens before school. One Tuesday, he noticed that one hen, Speckle, was not eating. He watched her closely and saw her limping on her left leg. Instead of going straight to school, he ran to find his grandmother so she could call the vet.
questions.text: How do you know Darius cared about Speckle? Use details from the passage.
options: He skipped school to play outside.
He noticed Speckle was not eating and went to get help.
He asked his grandmother to cook breakfast.
He fed all the chickens extra food.
questions.explanation: The passage states that Darius noticed Speckle limping and ran to find his grandmother to call the vet, showing he paid close attention and took action to help.

questions.passage: A young crow was very thirsty. She found a tall pitcher with a little water at the bottom. Her beak could not reach it. She tried tipping the pitcher — it would not fall. Then she picked up pebbles one by one and dropped them into the pitcher until the water rose high enough for her to drink.
questions.text: What is the central message of this story?
options: Crows should not drink water from pitchers.
A clever solution can solve a difficult problem.
It is better to wait for help than to work alone.
Water is always hard to find in the wild.
questions.explanation: The crow solves the problem by thinking creatively and using pebbles, showing that a smart approach can overcome a difficult challenge.

questions.passage: Tomás was afraid to try out for the school play. His best friend, Lily, kept encouraging him every day at lunch. On the day of tryouts, Tomás almost turned around and went home. But he thought of Lily's words, took a deep breath, and walked onto the stage.
questions.text: How do Lily's actions affect what Tomás does?
options: Lily's encouragement gives Tomás the courage to try out.
Lily signs Tomás up for the play without asking him.
Lily performs in the play so Tomás does not have to.
Lily tells Tomás the tryouts are not important.
questions.explanation: Lily's daily encouragement is what Tomás remembers just before he walks onto the stage, directly influencing his decision to go through with the tryout.

questions.passage: After the big win, the whole team was walking on air. They cheered, hugged, and laughed all the way back to the locker room.
questions.text: What does 'walking on air' mean in this passage?
options: The team was floating above the ground.
The team was moving very slowly.
The team was feeling extremely happy.
The team was tired after the game.
questions.explanation: 'Walking on air' is a nonliteral expression meaning feeling overjoyed or elated, which fits the context of the team celebrating a win.

questions.passage: Chapter 1 introduced Zara on her first day at a new school. Chapter 2 showed Zara making one friend, a girl named Priya. In Chapter 3, Priya invited Zara to her art club, and Zara finally felt like she belonged.
questions.text: How does Chapter 3 build on what happened in the earlier chapters?
options: Chapter 3 introduces a new character who replaces Priya.
Chapter 3 shows Zara going back to her old school.
Chapter 3 resolves the problem set up in Chapter 1 by showing Zara finding her place.
Chapter 3 starts a completely new story about an art club.
questions.explanation: Zara's problem in Chapter 1 was feeling out of place; Chapter 3 resolves this when she joins the art club and feels she belongs, completing the story's arc.

questions.passage: Leo thought the camping trip sounded boring. He did not say anything to his parents, but he wished he could stay home and read his books instead. Once they arrived at the lake, though, he saw a family of ducks, and a small smile crossed his face.
questions.text: Which statement best describes Leo's point of view at the start of the story?
options: Leo is excited to go camping.
Leo is frightened of the ducks.
Leo does not want to go camping.
Leo loves spending time with his parents.
questions.explanation: The passage states Leo thought camping sounded boring and wished he could stay home, showing he did not want to go.

questions.passage: Sea otters spend most of their lives floating on their backs in the ocean. They use their chests as tables to crack open shellfish for food. To keep from drifting apart while they sleep, otters hold hands with each other in groups called rafts.
questions.text: According to the passage, why do sea otters hold hands?
options: To scare away predators together.
To keep from drifting apart while they sleep.
To help each other crack open shellfish.
To stay warm in cold water.
questions.explanation: The passage states directly that otters hold hands to keep from drifting apart while they sleep.

questions.passage: Before a caterpillar can become a butterfly, it must go through several stages. First, a butterfly lays an egg on a leaf. Then, a caterpillar hatches from the egg and spends weeks eating and growing. Next, the caterpillar forms a protective shell called a chrysalis. Finally, after about two weeks inside, a butterfly emerges.
questions.text: What happens right AFTER the caterpillar hatches?
options: It forms a chrysalis.
It lays eggs on a leaf.
It eats and grows for weeks.
It becomes a butterfly.
questions.explanation: According to the sequence in the passage, after the caterpillar hatches it spends weeks eating and growing before forming a chrysalis.

questions.passage: Scientists who study volcanoes are called volcanologists. They use special tools to measure heat and gases near a volcano. Their research helps communities predict when an eruption might happen, giving people time to evacuate safely.
questions.text: What does the word 'evacuate' most likely mean in this passage?
options: Study a dangerous area closely.
Repair buildings after damage.
Leave a dangerous place to be safe.
Signal for help using special tools.
questions.explanation: The passage says evacuating gives people time to leave before an eruption, so 'evacuate' means to leave a dangerous place for safety.

questions.passage: Drinking enough water is important for your health. Without enough water, your body cannot carry nutrients to your cells. You may also feel tired or have trouble thinking clearly. That is why doctors recommend drinking at least eight cups of water each day.
questions.text: How does the last sentence connect to the sentences before it?
options: It introduces a brand-new topic about doctors.
It gives a recommendation based on the problems described earlier.
It contradicts the idea that water is important.
It provides an example of someone who was dehydrated.
questions.explanation: After describing what happens when you don't drink enough water, the last sentence provides a doctor's recommendation to prevent those problems.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The playful puppy ran quickly across the yard,' which word is an adverb?
options: playful
puppy
quickly
yard
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' is an adverb because it modifies the verb 'ran' and tells how the puppy ran.

questions.text: In the sentence 'She gave him a shiny trophy,' what part of speech is 'shiny'?
options: Noun
Verb
Adverb
Adjective
questions.explanation: 'Shiny' is an adjective because it describes the noun 'trophy.'

questions.text: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: The rain fell all afternoon.
Running through the puddles was fun.
Maya loves soccer, but her brother prefers basketball.
Because the game was canceled, we went home.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction; 'Maya loves soccer, but her brother prefers basketball' contains two complete thoughts joined by 'but.'

questions.text: Which word is spelled correctly?
options: freind
frend
friend
freend
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'friend.' Remember the rule: 'i before e except after c' applies here.

questions.passage: After two weeks without rain, the garden soil was parched and cracked. The gardener dragged a long hose across the lawn and began to water every row.
questions.text: What does the word 'parched' most likely mean based on the sentence?
options: Rich and dark
Extremely dry
Freshly dug
Full of worms
questions.explanation: The clue 'two weeks without rain' and 'cracked' tells you the soil was extremely dry, which is what 'parched' means.

questions.text: The prefix 'un-' means 'not.' What does the word 'unhappy' mean?
options: Very happy
Happy again
Not happy
A little happy
questions.explanation: The prefix 'un-' means 'not,' so 'unhappy' means not happy.

questions.text: The suffix '-ness' turns an adjective into a noun. What does the word 'kindness' mean?
options: To act in a kind way
The state or quality of being kind
Not kind at all
Someone who is kind
questions.explanation: The suffix '-ness' means 'the state or quality of,' so 'kindness' means the state or quality of being kind.

questions.text: Your teacher says, 'It's raining cats and dogs outside!' What does this idiom mean?
options: Cats and dogs are falling from the sky.
The animals are playing in the rain.
It is raining very heavily.
It is a light drizzle.
questions.explanation: 'Raining cats and dogs' is an idiom meaning it is raining very hard; no animals are actually falling.

questions.text: Which word can be broken into the roots 'tele-' (far away) and 'scope' (to see or watch)?
options: Telescope
Telephone
Television
Telegram
questions.explanation: 'Telescope' combines 'tele-' (far away) and '-scope' (to see), meaning an instrument for viewing things far away. Decoding word parts helps readers figure out meaning.

questions.passage: Benjamin Franklin wanted to prove that lightning was electricity. He flew a kite during a thunderstorm with a metal key attached to the string. When lightning struck near the kite, a spark jumped from the key to his hand. Because of this experiment, scientists began to understand the electrical nature of lightning.
questions.text: What was the CAUSE of scientists better understanding lightning?
options: Franklin built the first lightning rod for a church steeple.
Franklin's kite experiment showed that lightning was electrical.
A thunderstorm destroyed Franklin's laboratory.
Franklin published a book about weather patterns.
questions.explanation: The passage states that because of Franklin's kite experiment, scientists began to understand the electrical nature of lightning, making the experiment the cause.
